prompt: Implement the Command pattern with undo: append and deleteLast must each create an EditCommand that knows how to reverse itself, and undo() pops the most recent one off the history.
explanation: A command object bundles an action with everything needed to reverse it. append remembers the text it added so undo can cut the same number of characters off the end; deleteLast captures the characters it removed before removing them, so undo can put them back. Pushing commands onto a Deque used as a stack makes undo() simply pop the newest command and call its undo().
hints: An anonymous class -- new EditCommand() { ... } -- can capture the method parameter and any value you compute before creating it.
For deleteLast, work out the substring you are about to remove BEFORE removing it, and store it for undo.
Clamp n with Math.min(n, text.length()) so deleting more characters than exist is not an error, and use history.push / history.pop for the stack.
